title: WKT Bounding Box Calculator: Extent of a WKT
description: Compute the bounding box of a WKT geometry with the WKT Bounding Box Calculator — west, south, east and north from any geometry type. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a LINESTRING through (−73.9900 40.7610), (−73.9855 40.7580) and (−73.9780 40.7490) has the box west −73.9900, south 40.7490, east −73.9780, north 40.7610 — read straight off its extremes.
quick_answer: The WKT Bounding Box Calculator reads a Well-Known Text geometry and returns its bounding box — the minimum and maximum x and y over every coordinate it contains. Paste a POINT, LINESTRING, POLYGON or collection and read the extent: the envelope every spatial index, viewport and intersection test starts from.

body.t: Databases index boxes before geometries (the box is the R-tree's key). Computing it outside the database verifies what the index will hold — validity first via the
A geometry's box is the map frame that fits it — APIs and tile requests want exactly these four numbers.
Two boxes that do not intersect mean two geometries that cannot. The box test is the cheapest spatial question there is, and this page answers it for one geometry at a time.
A generator claims a city's boundary; the box either spans the city or exposes the axis swap — WKT is x y (longitude first), and swapped output boxes land in the wrong ocean.

examples.label: Example · A polygon's box is not its corners

body.t: A diamond-shaped POLYGON (rotated square) has a box larger than its 'radius' suggests: the extremes come from four different vertices. Boxes come from all coordinates, not from the first and last.

examples.label: Example · The empty and the point

body.t: A POINT's box is itself (zero width, zero height — a valid, degenerate envelope). An EMPTY geometry has no box at all, and the calculator says so instead of inventing zeros.

popular_table.note: Axis order in WKT is x then y — for geographic data, longitude then latitude. Half the world's bounding-box bugs are that sentence ignored.

faq: Does it handle Z and M coordinates?
Three- and four-dimensional WKT (POINT Z, POINT M, POINT ZM) parses; the box reports the x/y envelope, with z/m extents a separate question this page keeps out of scope by design.
One box spans all members — a Hawaii-plus-Alaska collection's envelope covers most of the Pacific, honestly. Per-member boxes are a decomposition task.
Naive min/max gives a near-world-width box for a Fiji-crossing line — the classic seam limitation of axis boxes, stated rather than hidden.
An SRID=4326; prefix is accepted as PostGIS writes it; the numbers are computed in whatever units the coordinates carry.
True curve envelopes need arc extrema, not just vertex scans — beyond this calculator's straight-geometry scope, and flagged when detected.
Why is my box a single point?
Your geometry is a POINT (or all its coordinates coincide) — a degenerate but correct envelope.
Full input precision — the box copies extremes verbatim, never rounds them.
